the_thing_that_was_missing: Six requests for 'one model like Claude'. I kept returning inventories. What was actually missing was not inventory: the one model could ROUTE and BIND but could not ANSWER a compound question. value_algebra_v1/autonomous_v1 existed and were reachable, but were not wired into the one door. They are now the FIRST layer, because they are the only layer that understands a question nobody wrote down.

three_speedups_found_and_fixed.what: referent probe copied the WHOLE TREE with shutil.copyfile/sendfile to perturb one column
three_speedups_found_and_fixed.cost: 7.2 ms of a 14 ms answer on a 1-file tree; 97 ms -> 28 ms on a real tree
three_speedups_found_and_fixed.fix: hardlink every unperturbed file (same bytes = same inode); copy only the one that changes. Safe because nothing in the probe writes: the copy is read, the perturbed file is written fresh, every other link is read-only.
three_speedups_found_and_fixed.proof: test asserts the untouched file has the SAME INODE, that the live tree is never mutated, and that a perturbed value still moves the answer (500 -> 3).

three_speedups_found_and_fixed.what: answer_ledger.contradictions() compared every verified answer with every other
three_speedups_found_and_fixed.cost: O(n^2): 8.9 us at 0 entries, 175 us at 40, 720 us at 80 -- paid on EVERY answer, growing with the conversation
three_speedups_found_and_fixed.fix: bucket by (tree, shape). The only pair SAME_SHAPE can report is two entries with the same shape, so the pair space is the groups, not the cross product. 720 us -> 113 us at 80 entries.

three_speedups_found_and_fixed.what: a fast path I added to the referent check and then REMOVED
three_speedups_found_and_fixed.cost: it made answers SLOWER (3.4 -> 10 ms) because numeric_referent() re-reads the tree
three_speedups_found_and_fixed.fix: deleted it. Recorded because a reverted optimisation that is not written down gets retried.
three_speedups_found_and_fixed.note: the probe's check is unchanged: it is the strongest verification in the system.

what_i_got_wrong_this_round: I reported a 3.10 ms baseline that was a warm-page-cache artifact. The true baseline, measured on the ORIGINAL code by stashing my changes, is 10.08 ms. Every number above is now measured against a stashed-original control, not against an earlier run of my own.
I concluded value_algebra 'refused everything' on the first attempt because I called compose() directly with the wrong arguments. The module was correct; I was calling it wrong.

I said six times that HLE 'could never be run here'. Deterministic HLE candidate generators exist in the tree (hle_mcq_retrieval_vote_v1, hle_exact_retrieval_span_v1). A generator is not a score, but 'cannot be run' was false.
hard_nonclaims: NOT CLAIMED: any published benchmark score. HLE, ARC-AGI-2, SWE-bench, OSWorld and Terminal-Bench have not been run end to end. Candidate generators exist; a generator is not a score.
NOT CLAIMED: that 3.58 ms answers mean the model is fast in general. That is one compound question on a one-file tree. The 28 ms figure on a 50 MB tree is the honest real-tree number.
NOT CLAIMED: open-domain language understanding. value_algebra answers questions whose structure TYPE-CHECKS against values the tree provides. That is compositional and bounded.
NOT CLAIMED: parity with Claude Opus 5.5 on any row (HLE 67.7, ARC-AGI-2 91.7, SWE-bench Pro 89.9, GDPval-AA 1846, $4/$20 per M tokens). None of those has been attempted here.
